acts.18.p1.b1.text: After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.

acts.18.p1.b2.text: There he found a Jew named Aquila, … who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla … Paul went to visit them,

acts.18.p1.b3.text: and he stayed and worked with them because they were tentmakers by trade, just as he was.

acts.18.p1.b4.text: Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue, trying to persuade Jews and Greeks alike.

acts.18.p2.b5.text: And when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself fully to the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.

acts.18.p2.b6.text: “Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent of it. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.”

acts.18.p2.b7.text: So Paul left the synagogue and went next door to the house of Titus Justus, a worshiper of God.

acts.18.p2.b8.text: Crispus, the synagogue leader, and his whole household believed in the Lord. And many of the Corinthians who heard the message believed and were baptized.

acts.18.p3.b9.text: One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision:

acts.18.p3.b10.text: “Do not be afraid; keep on speaking; do not be silent. For I am with you and no one will lay a hand on you,

acts.18.p3.b11.text: because I have many people in this city.”

acts.18.p3.b12.text: So Paul stayed for a year and a half, teaching the word of God among the Corinthians.

acts.18.p4.b13.text: While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews coordinated an attack on Paul and brought him before the judgment seat.

acts.18.p4.b14.text: “This man is persuading the people to worship God in ways contrary to the law,”

acts.18.p4.b15.text: But just as Paul was about to speak, Gallio told the Jews,

acts.18.p4.b16.text: But since it is a dispute about words and names and your own law, settle it yourselves. I refuse to be a judge of such things.”

acts.18.p5.b17.text: And he drove them away from the judgment seat.

acts.18.p5.b18.text: At this, the crowd seized Sosthenes the synagogue leader and beat him in front of the judgment seat.

acts.18.p5.b19.text: But none of this was of concern to Gallio.

acts.18.p6.b20.text: Paul remained in Corinth for quite some time before saying goodbye to the brothers.

acts.18.p6.b21.text: and then he sailed for Syria, accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila.

acts.18.p6.b22.text: He had his head shaved in Cenchrea to keep a vow he had made,

acts.18.p7.b23.text: When they reached Ephesus, Paul parted ways with Priscilla and Aquila.

acts.18.p7.b24.text: He himself went into the synagogue there and reasoned with the Jews. When they asked him to stay for a while longer, he declined.

acts.18.p7.b25.text: “I will come back to you if God is willing.”

acts.18.p7.b26.text: And he set sail from Ephesus.

acts.18.p8.b27.text: When Paul had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church at Jerusalem.

acts.18.p8.b28.text: Then he went down to Antioch. After Paul had spent some time in Antioch,

acts.18.p8.b29.text: he traveled from place to place throughout the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.

acts.18.p9.b30.text: Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, well versed in the Scriptures.

acts.18.p9.b31.text: He had been instructed in the way of the Lord and was fervent in spirit. He spoke and taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.

acts.18.p9.b32.text: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him,

acts.18.p9.b33.text: they took him in and explained to him the way of God more accurately.

acts.18.p10.b34.text: When Apollos resolved to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there to welcome him.

acts.18.p10.b35.text: On his arrival, he was a great help to those who by grace had believed.

acts.18.p10.b36.text: For he powerfully refuted the Jews in public debate, proving from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.
